extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers in zoology/taxonomy, particularly specialists in freshwater sponge (Spongillidae) identification
extracted.subtask_description: A taxonomic key and species descriptions for the Indian Spongillidæ (freshwater sponges), giving diagnostic morphological characters (gemmules, spicules, skeleton, colour, etc.) to identify genera, subgenera and species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order Halichondrina definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Siliceous monaxon sponges in which the horny skeleton is much reduced or absent and the spicular skeleton is more or less definitely reticulate. The microscleres are usually rod-like and rarely have more than one main axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a higher-level diagnostic definition used to place taxa into the order Halichondrina based on skeletal structure and microsclere morphology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Spongillidae diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Freshwater Halichondrina which at certain seasons produce gemmules armed with peculiar microscleres. Two distinct kinds of microsclere are often present ... There is always at least a trace of a subdermal cavity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of gemmules with characteristic microscleres and at least a trace of subdermal cavity are required to recognize members of Spongillidae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision into Spongillinæ (Euspongillinæ) vs Meyeninæ (Ephydatiinæ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many authors divide the Spongillidæ into two subfamilies: Spongillinæ (or Euspongillinæ), in which the gemmule-spicules have no transverse rotulæ, and Meyeninæ (or Ephydatiinæ), in which they have rotulæ at one or both ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence vs absence of transverse rotulæ on gemmule-spicules as the primary character to separate these subfamilies, though transitions may be gradual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-level key: microscleres without transverse disks -> Spongilla
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscleres without transverse disks. Microscleres of the parenchyma similar in general structure to those of the gemmule; the latter without comb-like vertical rows of spines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parenchyma microscleres resemble gemmule microscleres and no comb-like rows of spines occur on the gemmule-spicules, assign to Spongilla (see p. 67).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-level key: gemmule microscleres with comb-like vertical rows of spines -> Pectispongilla
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscleres without transverse disks, but microscleres of the gemmule with comb-like vertical rows of spines at both ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comb-like vertical rows of spines on gemmule microscleres are diagnostic of Pectispongilla (see p. 106).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-level key: some or all microscleres birotulate (Ephydatia/Dosilia/Trochospongilla/Corvospongilla distinctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some or all of the microscleres birotulate (birotulate microscleres of one kind only). Various patterns of rotules and parenchyma microscleres distinguish Ephydatia, Dosilia, Trochospongilla, and Corvospongilla.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the following distinctions: Ephydatia — gemmule microscleres birotulate, rotules serrated or strongly sinuous, parenchyma spicules usually absent; Dosilia — gemmule microscleres as in Ephydatia but parenchyma microscleres numerous shafts meeting in central nodule; Trochospongilla — as Ephydatia but rotulæ of gemmule-spicules have smooth edges; Corvospongilla — gemmule microscleres without rotulæ, parenchyma birotulate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-level key: gemmule microscleres with basal rotule and shaft ending in knob -> Tubella
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscleres of the gemmule with a well-developed basal rotule and a vertical shaft ending above in a mere knob.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This combination of a basal rotule plus a knobbed shaft is diagnostic of Tubella (see p. 120).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenus Euspongilla diagnostic envelope
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules covered with a thick, apparently granular pneumatic coat. A delicate membrane often occurs outside this coat, but it is never thick or horny. The gemmules usually lie free in the sponge but sometimes adhere to its support; the skeleton-spicules are never very stout and the skeleton is always delicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the presence of a thick granular pneumatic coat on gemmules and a delicate skeleton (not stout spicules) to recognize Euspongilla; species in the subgenus are distinguished by the sum of small peculiarities rather than a single character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species key: gemmule with thick granular pneumatic coat; no foraminal tubule; bright green soft sponge -> S. lacustris
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmule provided with a thick, apparently granular pneumatic coat in which the gemmule-spicules are arranged tangentially or vertically. No foraminal tubule. Sponge bright green, soft and compressible when fresh, very fragile when dry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bright green colour and soft/compressible texture when fresh, plus the described gemmule coat and lack of foraminal tubule, identify S. lacustris.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species key: gemmule with thick granular pneumatic coat; no foraminal tubule; white/grey hard sponge -> S. alba
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmule with thick granular pneumatic coat; no foraminal tubule. Sponge white or grey, hard both fresh and dry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour and firmness (white/grey and hard) with the indicated gemmule coat and absence of foraminal tubule diagnose S. alba.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species key: foraminal tubule present; skeleton-spicules smooth; gemmules free; gemmule-spicules tangential/horizontal -> S. proliferens
rubrics_metrics.description: A foraminal tubule present. Skeleton-spicules smooth. Gemmules free; gemmule-spicules arranged tangentially and horizontally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of a foraminal tubule combined with smooth skeleton-spicules and tangential/horizontal gemmule-spicule arrangement indicates S. proliferens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species key: foraminal tubule present; skeleton-spicules smooth; gemmule-spicules vertical single series -> S. hemephydatia
rubrics_metrics.description: A foraminal tubule present. Skeleton-spicules smooth. Gemmules free; gemmule-spicules arranged vertically or nearly so in a single series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vertical single-series arrangement of gemmule-spicules with a foraminal tubule and smooth skeleton-spicules identifies S. hemephydatia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species key: foraminal tubule present; skeleton-spicules smooth; gemmules firmly fixed; spicules almost vertical, often >1 series -> S. travancorica
rubrics_metrics.description: A foraminal tubule present. Skeleton-spicules smooth. Gemmules firmly fixed to the support of the sponge; gemmule-spicules almost vertical, irregularly arranged, as a rule in more than one series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gemmmules firmly attached and multi-series/irregular vertical spicule arrangement with smooth skeleton-spicules indicate S. travancorica.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species key: foraminal tubule present; skeleton-spicules spiny/irregular; gemmule-spicules tangential/horizontal without rudimentary rotules -> S. cinerea
rubrics_metrics.description: A foraminal tubule present. Skeleton-spicules spiny or irregular in outline. Gemmule-spicules tangential and horizontal, without rudimentary rotules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spiny/irregular skeleton-spicules and tangential/horizontal gemmule-spicules with no rudimentary rotules identify S. cinerea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species key: foraminal tubule present; skeleton-spicules spiny/irregular; gemmule-spicules vertical often with rudimentary rotules -> S. crateriformis
rubrics_metrics.description: A foraminal tubule present. Skeleton-spicules spiny or irregular in outline. Gemmule-spicules vertical or nearly so, often with rudimentary rotules at the tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vertical gemmule-spicules often showing rudimentary rotules combined with spiny/irregular skeleton-spicules and a foraminal tubule indicate S. crateriformis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenus Eunapius diagnostic envelope
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules surrounded in several layers by distinct polygonal air-spaces with chitinous walls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This character (polygonal cellular pneumatic coat) defines the subgenus Eunapius; further species distinctions depend on gemmule number (single, paired, groups) and skeleton hardness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eunapius: gemmules single; skeleton- and gemmule-spicules smooth and pointed, not very stout -> S. carteri
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules single. Skeleton- and gemmule-spicules smooth, pointed, not very stout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single gemmules in a polygonal cellular coat with smooth, slender spicules indicate S. carteri.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eunapius: gemmules paired; skeleton friable; slender skeleton-spicules -> S. gemina (var.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules bound together in pairs. Skeleton friable; skeleton-spicules slender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paired gemmules with a friable skeleton and slender spicules characterize the named variety/species related to S. gemina.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eunapius: gemmules in groups/pavement-layer; skeleton friable & slender -> S. fragilis
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules bound together in free groups of more than two or forming a 'pavement-layer' at the base of the sponge. Skeleton friable; skeleton-spicules slender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouped gemmules forming pavement-layers with a friable skeleton indicate S. fragilis (or related forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eunapius: gemmules in groups/pavement-layer; skeleton very hard/resistant; spicules stout -> S. crassissima
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules bound together in free groups or pavement-layer. Skeleton very hard and resistant; skeleton-spicules stout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouped gemmules with a very hard, resistant skeleton and stout spicules identify S. crassissima (and varieties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenus Stratospongilla diagnostic envelope
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules without or with irregular pneumatic coat, covered by a chitinous membrane or membranes in which the gemmule-spicules lie parallel to the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of chitinous membrane(s) with gemmule-spicules parallel to the surface indicates Stratospongilla; further separation depends on skeleton-spicule outline (spiny/irregular vs smooth) and number of membranes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stratospongilla: skeleton-spicules spiny/irregular; blunt skeleton-spicules; gemmules covered by single chitinous membrane -> S. indica
rubrics_metrics.description: Skeleton-spicules spiny or irregular in outline. Skeleton-spicules blunt; gemmules covered by a single chitinous membrane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blunt, spiny/irregular skeleton-spicules plus a single chitinous membrane on the gemmules denote S. indica.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stratospongilla: skeleton-spicules spiny/irregular; sharp skeleton-spicules; gemmules covered by two chitinous membranes -> S. bombayensis
rubrics_metrics.description: Skeleton-spicules spiny or irregular; skeleton-spicules sharp; gemmules covered by two chitinous membranes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharp spiny skeleton-spicules with gemmules enclosed in two chitinous membranes indicate S. bombayensis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stratospongilla: skeleton-spicules smooth; spicules sharp; gemmule-spicules very irregular -> S. ultima
rubrics_metrics.description: Skeleton-spicules smooth. Skeleton-spicules sharp; gemmule-spicules very irregular in form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smooth sharp skeleton-spicules combined with very irregular gemmule-spicules indicate S. ultima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species-level profile: Spongilla lacustris (morphological description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponge soft and easily compressed, very brittle when dry, usually consisting of a flat or rounded basal portion and long free cylindrical drooping branches; colour bright green in strong light, dirty flesh-colour in shade. Oscula star-shaped with furrows; oscular collars well developed. Skeleton reticulate, loose, with definite radiating and transverse fibres held together by a small quantity of spongin; fibres slender but not extremely so. Skeleton-spicules smooth, sharply pointed, long, slender. Flesh-spicules slender, covered with small spines, sharply pointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This morphological suite is diagnostic for S. lacustris; use the combination of habit (branches drooping), coloration (bright green in light), oscular morphology, skeleton reticulation and spicule characters to confirm identification.
